label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, these respondents consistently score above moderate thresholds across all three psychological distress measures. The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests individuals who may be heavily engaged in digital work or social environments yet experience significant emotional isolation and mental health challenges.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness despite likely digital connectivity
Shows the highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ~2.17)
Engages in prolonged daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
Highly educated yet experiencing compounded psychological distress
tone: Strained and overwhelmed; reflects a pattern of persistent emotional burden beneath a high-functioning exterior

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or online activity
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near the low end of the scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen time (1–3 hours)
Represents a relatively large and stable subgroup (n = 150 in training split)
tone: Calm, stable, and emotionally resilient with an overall sense of psychological well-being

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the emotional distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) well below clinical thresholds
Relatively limited daily screen time (1–3 hours), suggesting restrained digital engagement
Disconnect between social isolation feelings and affective symptom severity
tone: Quietly detached yet emotionally stable; reflective rather than distressed
